$comment: Rule catalog — domains, quantifiers, assumptions, and symbolic manipulation. Standards 5, 6, 11, 13, 20.

rules.title: Every claim states its domain
rules.description: Every claim at HYPOTHESIS rank or above carries a non-empty Domain field naming the set each free variable ranges over.
rules.rationale: A claim proved only for squarefree n and stated for all n is a different theorem, and the difference is invisible unless the domain is written down.
rules.remediation: Add the Domain field, including any restriction the proof relies on.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that a domain was stated. Whether the stated domain is the one the proof actually covers requires reading the proof, and is rigor.domain-restrictions-ignored.

rules.title: Every claim states its quantifier structure
rules.description: Every claim at HYPOTHESIS rank or above carries a non-empty Quantifiers field, including the order of alternating quantifiers and any sufficiency qualifier.
rules.rationale: Reordering two quantifiers produces an unrelated claim, and the reordering is where the real errors live rather than in the property being quantified.
rules.remediation: Add the Quantifiers field. Where the claim is uniform in a parameter, say so; uniformity used in a proof and not stated is a hidden strengthening.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the field was filled in. It does not parse the quantifier structure or compare it against the proof.

rules.title: Every claim declares its assumptions
rules.description: Every claim at HYPOTHESIS rank or above carries an Assumptions field; `none` is an acceptable value and an omitted field is not.
rules.rationale: An absent field and an empty field are different, and only one of them shows that the author considered the question.
rules.remediation: Add the Assumptions field listing every statement the claim relies on and does not establish, or `none`.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the field exists. Every downstream check that uses assumptions operates on what was declared; an assumption nobody wrote down is invisible to all of them.

rules.title: Unproved statements relied upon are registered
rules.description: Every identifier appearing in an Assumptions field resolves to a ledger entry or an external reference, rather than being named only in prose.
rules.rationale: An unproved statement absorbed into prose as though it were established is a hidden conjecture; registering it gives it a status that downstream checks can read.
rules.remediation: Register the statement in the ledger as CONJECTURE, HYPOTHESIS, or UNRESOLVED_CLAIM, and reference it by identifier.
rules.$assuranceNote: Checks that declared assumptions resolve. It cannot find an assumption that was never declared.

rules.title: Symbolic steps state their validity conditions
rules.description: Each nontrivial manipulation — cancellation, root extraction, rearrangement, matrix inversion — states the condition under which it is valid, and that condition is a discharged obligation or a declared assumption.
rules.rationale: Algebra is where proofs fail quietly: each step is locally correct under a condition that was never stated, and the resulting proof survives many readings.
rules.remediation: For each step in Standard 13 R1's table that the proof uses, record the condition as an obligation and discharge it.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector, deliberately. A rule flagging every division would produce noise a project would suppress, and a suppressed rule still counts in coverage. Established by a mathematician or by a proof assistant that refuses the step.

rules.title: An unproved assumption is never hidden
rules.description: A result relies on a statement that is neither proved nor declared in its Assumptions field.
rules.rationale: The most damaging unproved statement in a piece of research is the one nobody wrote down, and it is usually not a grand conjecture but a step that felt obvious.
rules.remediation: Declare the assumption and register it with an honest status; the claim relying on it is then capped at CONDITIONAL_THEOREM until the assumption is proved.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector and there cannot be one: the whole content of the rule is about something absent from the record. Established by a mathematician reading the proof and asking what it uses.

rules.title: Domain restrictions are never ignored
rules.description: A claim is stated or used on a domain larger than the one its proof covers.
rules.rationale: The proof may be entirely correct on its actual domain; the overstatement is in where the result is applied, which is invisible from the proof alone.
rules.remediation: Restate the claim on the domain the proof covers, and re-examine every use of it outside that domain.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. rigor.explicit-domain establishes that a domain was stated; comparing it against the proof's actual coverage is mathematics.

rules.title: Never divide without establishing the nonzero condition
rules.description: A proof divides by, or cancels, an expression without establishing that the expression is non-zero throughout the domain.
rules.rationale: The argument is fine for generic values and the theorem claims all values; the failure is at exactly the degenerate cases Standard 9 is about.
rules.remediation: Record the non-vanishing as a proof obligation and discharge it, or exclude the vanishing case from the domain.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. Whether a denominator can vanish on the domain is the mathematics, not a property of the text.

rules.title: Never interchange limits without justification
rules.description: A proof exchanges the order of limits, sums, derivatives, or integrals without the uniformity, convergence, or domination hypothesis that makes the exchange valid.
rules.rationale: The failure occurs where convergence is not uniform, which is typically nowhere visible in the formulas and requires knowing something about the functions involved.
rules.remediation: Record the justifying hypothesis as a proof obligation and discharge it, citing the theorem that licenses the interchange.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. Established by a mathematician, or by formalising the step in a proof assistant, which cannot proceed without the hypothesis.

rules.title: Without loss of generality must not lose generality
rules.description: A WLOG reduction discards a case that is not in fact equivalent to the case kept, by a symmetry that is assumed rather than established.
rules.rationale: The idiom launders an unproved symmetry past reviewers: it announces that a reduction is obvious, which is exactly when nobody checks it.
rules.remediation: State the symmetry or reduction as an obligation and discharge it, or handle the discarded case explicitly.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. Established by a reviewer checking that the claimed symmetry holds.

rules.title: Almost-all results are never treated as universal
rules.description: A density-one, almost-everywhere, generic, or probability-one result is used or restated as holding for all cases, or at a particular case of interest.
rules.rationale: Unlike the finite-to-infinite inference, the underlying theorem here is entirely correct. The exceptional set is exactly what the theorem declined to control, and the point of interest may lie in it.
rules.remediation: Restate the claim with its qualifier intact, and where a particular case is needed, prove that it lies outside the exceptional set.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. rigor.explicit-quantifiers requires the qualifier to be recorded; noticing that a later passage dropped it is review.

rules.title: A symbol carries one meaning throughout an argument
rules.description: The same symbol or term is used with two meanings within one argument, so that each step is valid under some reading and no single consistent reading validates all of them.
rules.rationale: Notably common in machine-generated proofs, which have no persistent sense of what a symbol was introduced to mean, and hard to see on reading because every individual line is correct.
rules.remediation: Fix one meaning per symbol in the definitions, rename the collision, and recheck each step under the single reading.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. Establishing it requires tracking what each symbol denotes at each step, which is reading the mathematics.
